638: export async function persistAndCompleteStep(
639: 	outcome: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof runAgentStep>>,
640: ): Promise<ExecutionRunResult> {
641: 	if (outcome.status === "skipped") {
642: 		return {
643: 			workflowId: outcome.workflowId,
644: 			executionId: outcome.executionId,
645: 			status: "skipped",
646: 			summary: "",
647: 			stepCount: 0,
648: 			toolCount: 0,
649: 		};
650: 	}
651: 	const execution = await workflowService.getExecution(outcome.executionId);
652: 	if (
653: 		execution &&
654: 		(execution.status === "completed" ||
655: 			execution.status === "failed" ||
656: 			execution.status === "cancelled" ||
657: 			execution.status === "sleeping" ||
658: 			execution.status === "waiting")
659: 	) {
660: 		return {
661: 			workflowId: outcome.workflowId,
662: 			executionId: outcome.executionId,
663: 			status: "skipped",
664: 			summary: "",
665: 			stepCount: 0,
666: 			toolCount: 0,
667: 		};
668: 	}
669: 	const result = outcome.result;
670: 	if (!result) {
671: 		throw new NonRetriableError(
672: 			`No agent result for execution: ${outcome.executionId}`,
673: 		);
674: 	}
675: 	const toolCallCount = result.steps.reduce(
676: 		(count, step) => count + step.toolCalls.length,
677: 		0,
678: 	);
679: 	await workflowService.recordSteps({
680: 		executionId: outcome.executionId,
681: 		steps: result.steps,
682: 	});
683: 	let planEmitted = false;
684: 	let finalizedStatus:
685: 		| "completed"
686: 		| "sleeping"
687: 		| "waiting"
688: 		| "cancelled"
689: 		| "failed"
690: 		| "awaiting_approval" = "completed";
691: 	if (outcome.mode === "planning") {
692: 		const plan = extractPlan(result.text);
693: 		if (plan) {
694: 			await workflowService.updatePlan(outcome.workflowId, plan);
695: 			planEmitted = true;
696: 		}
697: 		await workflowService.completeExecution({
698: 			executionId: outcome.executionId,
699: 		});
700: 	} else {
701: 		const execution = await workflowService.getExecution(outcome.executionId);
702: 		const requiredApprovals = execution
703: 			? result.pendingApprovals.filter(
704: 					(p) => p.input !== undefined && p.input !== null,
705: 				)
706: 			: [];
707: 		let heldForApproval = false;
708: 		if (execution && requiredApprovals.length > 0) {
709: 			const created = await workflowService.recordApprovalRequests(
710: 				outcome.workflowId,
711: 				outcome.executionId,
712: 				requiredApprovals.map((p) => ({
713: 					toolName: p.toolName,
714: 					input: p.input,
715: 				})),
716: 			);
717: 			if (created.length > 0) {
718: 				await workflowService.holdExecutionForApproval(
719: 					outcome.executionId,
720: 					`Awaiting approval for: ${[...new Set(created.map((a) => a.toolName))].join(", ")}`,
721: 				);
722: 				heldForApproval = true;
723: 			}
724: 		}
725: 		const decision = extractDecision(result.text);
726: 		if (decision && execution && !heldForApproval) {
727: 			const maxSleepMs = env.EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS * 1000;
728: 			if (
729: 				decision.action === "sleep" &&
730: 				decision.sleepUntil &&
731: 				decision.sleepUntil.getTime() - Date.now() > maxSleepMs
732: 			) {
733: 				decision.sleepUntil = new Date(Date.now() + maxSleepMs);
734: 			}
735: 			const applied = await workflowService.applyDecision({
736: 				workflowId: outcome.workflowId,
737: 				executionId: outcome.executionId,
738: 				decision,
739: 			});
740: 			finalizedStatus =
741: 				applied.action === "sleep"
742: 					? "sleeping"
743: 					: applied.action === "stop"
744: 						? "cancelled"
745: 						: applied.action === "wait"
746: 							? "waiting"
747: 							: "completed";
748: 			if (applied.action === "sleep") {
749: 				const activity = await workflowService.getActivitySnapshot(
750: 					outcome.workflowId,
751: 				);
752: 				if (activity) {
753: 					await workflowService.updateActivitySnapshot(outcome.workflowId, {
754: 						...activity,
755: 						status: "sleeping",
756: 						currentActivity: `sleeping until ${decision.sleepUntil?.toISOString()}`,
757: 						updatedAt: new Date(),
758: 					});
759: 				}
760: 			}
761: 			if (applied.action === "notify" && applied.deliverables.length > 0) {
762: 				for (const deliverable of applied.deliverables) {
763: 					await inngest.send({
764: 						name: notificationPublishEvent,
765: 						data: { notificationId: deliverable.notificationId },
766: 					});
767: 				}
768: 			}
769: 			if (applied.action === "wait") {
770: 				const activity = await workflowService.getActivitySnapshot(
771: 					outcome.workflowId,
772: 				);
773: 				if (activity) {
774: 					await workflowService.updateActivitySnapshot(outcome.workflowId, {
775: 						...activity,
776: 						status: "waiting",
777: 						currentActivity: `waiting on webhook: ${decision.waitFor?.description}`,
778: 						updatedAt: new Date(),
779: 					});
780: 				}
781: 			}
782: 		} else if (heldForApproval) {
783: 			finalizedStatus = "awaiting_approval";
784: 			const heldActivity = await workflowService.getActivitySnapshot(
785: 				outcome.workflowId,
786: 			);
787: 			if (heldActivity) {
788: 				await workflowService.updateActivitySnapshot(outcome.workflowId, {
789: 					...heldActivity,
790: 					status: "awaiting_approval",
791: 					currentActivity: "waiting for user approval",
792: 					updatedAt: new Date(),
793: 				});
794: 			}
795: 		} else {
796: 			await workflowService.completeExecution({
797: 				executionId: outcome.executionId,
798: 			});
799: 		}
800: 	}
801: 	const activity = await workflowService.getActivitySnapshot(
802: 		outcome.workflowId,
803: 	);
804: 	if (activity) {
805: 		await workflowService.updateActivitySnapshot(outcome.workflowId, {
806: 			...activity,
807: 			status:
808: 				finalizedStatus === "sleeping"
809: 					? "sleeping"
810: 					: finalizedStatus === "waiting"
811: 						? "waiting"
812: 						: finalizedStatus === "awaiting_approval"
813: 							? "awaiting_approval"
814: 							: "completed",
815: 			currentActivity:
816: 				finalizedStatus === "awaiting_approval"
817: 					? "waiting for user approval"
818: 					: undefined,
819: 			updatedAt: new Date(),
820: 		});
821: 	}
822: 	const summary = result.text.slice(0, 500);
823: 	if (finalizedStatus === "completed" && outcome.recoveryContext) {
824: 		await workflowService.updateRecoveryResult(
825: 			outcome.executionId,
826: 			outcome.recoveryContext.attempt,
827: 			"completed",
828: 			{ failureCode: outcome.recoveryContext.failureCode },
829: 		);
830: 		await storeProceduralMemory(
831: 			outcome.workflowId,
832: 			outcome.executionId,
833: 			outcome.recoveryContext,
834: 		);
835: 	}
836: 	if (finalizedStatus === "completed") {
837: 		await storeEpisodicMemory(outcome.workflowId, outcome.executionId, summary);
838: 	}
839: 	return {
840: 		workflowId: outcome.workflowId,
841: 		executionId: outcome.executionId,
842: 		status: finalizedStatus,
843: 		summary,
844: 		stepCount: result.steps.length,
845: 		toolCount: toolCallCount,
846: 		planEmitted,
847: 	};
848: }

857: export const executionRun = inngest.createFunction(
858: 	{
859: 		id: "execution-run",
860: 		retries: 2,
861: 		triggers: [{ event: executionRunEvent }],
862: 		onFailure: async ({ event, error }) => {
863: 			const parsed = failureEventSchema.safeParse(event);
864: 			if (!parsed.success) {
865: 				return;
866: 			}
867: 			const { executionId } = parsed.data.data.event.data;
868: 			const execution = await workflowService.getExecution(executionId);
869: 			if (
870: 				!execution ||
871: 				execution.status === "completed" ||
872: 				execution.status === "failed" ||
873: 				execution.status === "cancelled"
874: 			) {
875: 				return;
876: 			}
877: 			const reason = (
878: 				parsed.data.data.error?.message ??
879: 				error.message ??
880: 				"execution failed unexpectedly"
881: 			).slice(0, 500);
882: 			const classification = classifyFailure({
883: 				code: parsed.data.data.error?.code,
884: 			});
885: 			const scheduled = await maybeScheduleRecovery(
886: 				parsed.data.data.event.data,
887: 				{
888: 					code: classification.failureCode ?? "EXECUTION_FAILED",
889: 					reason,
890: 				},
891: 			);
892: 			void scheduled;
893: 		},
894: 	},
895: 	async ({ event, step }) => {
896: 		const resolved = await step.run("resolve-execution-state", () =>
897: 			resolveExecutionState(event.data),
898: 		);

304:     // itemRects, so they need fresh rects when the row's height changes.

318:       setIsOtherMultiline(false);

322:       if (!el) return;

324:       el.style.height = `${el.scrollHeight}px`;

326:       // hard-coded 22px — so the flag stays correct at high browser

336:     // ── freeText auto-focus ─────────────────────────────────────

348:     // ── Animated height ──────────────────────────────────────────

371:       focusedIndexRef.current = focusedIndex;

383:     // ── Keyboard focus restoration across question changes ───────
384:     // The question content remounts on qId, which destroys the focused row and

399:         rowsContainerRef.current?.contains(document.activeElement) &&

402:         restoreFocusRef.current = true;

407:       restoreFocusRef.current = false;

526:         [qId]: {

529:           otherText: text,

536:     const handleSkip = useCallback(() => {
537:       if (!question) return;

539:         ...prev,
540:         [qId]: {

562:     // ── Keyboard shortcuts: 1-9 ──────────────────────────────────
563:     useEffect(() => {
564:       if (!question) return;
565:       const handler = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
566:         if (e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey || e.altKey) return;
567:         const target = e.target as HTMLElement | null;
568:         if (!target) return;
569:         const tag = target.tagName;
570:         if (tag === "INPUT" || tag === "TEXTAREA" || target.isContentEditable) return;
571:         // Only one mounted instance may answer this keypress (see
572:         // mountedInstances): the one containing focus, or the most recently
573:         // mounted one when focus sits outside every instance.
574:         const root = rootRef.current;
575:         if (!root) return;
576:         if (!root.contains(target)) {
577:           if (mountedInstances.some((el) => el !== root && el.contains(target)))
578:             return;
579:           // A focused element that WRAPS instances (a docs preview frame
580:           // holding keyboard scope — see click-to-focus) narrows the pick to
581:           // the instances inside it; focus on <body> wraps them all, which
582:           // degenerates to the original most-recently-mounted rule.
583:           const wrapped = mountedInstances.filter((el) => target.contains(el));
584:           const pool = wrapped.length > 0 ? wrapped : mountedInstances;
585:           if (pool[pool.length - 1] !== root) return;
586:         }
587:         const code = e.key;
588:         if (code < "1" || code > "9") return;
589:         const idx = parseInt(code, 10) - 1;
590:         if (idx >= 0 && idx < options.length) {
591:           e.preventDefault();
592:           const oid = optionKey(options[idx]!, idx);
593:           if (isMulti) handleMultiToggle(oid);
594:           else handleSingleSelect(oid);

596:           e.preventDefault();
597:           otherInputRef.current?.focus();
598:         }

601:       return () => document.removeEventListener("keydown", handler);
602:     }, [
603:       question,
604:       options,
605:       isMulti,
606:       allowOther,
607:       handleSingleSelect,
608:       handleMultiToggle,
609:     ]);

611:     // ── Keyboard navigation ──────────────────────────────────────
612:     // Up/Down move the highlight between rows using the SAME indicator as
613:     // mouse hover (activeIndex → bg-hover), so keyboard and pointer focus look
614:     // identical. Left = Back, Right = Skip. We stopPropagation on the arrows we
615:     // handle so the doc page's ←/→ page-change nav (a window listener) doesn't
616:     // also fire — important for multi-select, whose container is role="group"
617:     // (not "radiogroup") and so isn't auto-skipped by that handler.
618:     const focusRow = (idx: number) => {
619:       const el = rowsContainerRef.current?.querySelector(
620:         `[data-fluid-hover-index="${idx}"]`
621:       ) as HTMLElement | null;
622:       el?.focus();
623:     };

625:     const moveActive = useCallback(
626:       (next: number) => {
627:         setActiveIndex(next);
628:         // The Other row is a text field — focus the input directly so typing
629:         // works; everything else focuses the row for Enter/Space selection.
630:         if (allowOther && next === otherIndex) otherInputRef.current?.focus();
631:         else focusRow(next);
632:       },
633:       [allowOther, otherIndex, setActiveIndex]
634:     );

636:     const handleNavKey = (e: ReactKeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
637:       const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
638:       const isTextInput =
639:         target.tagName === "INPUT" ||
640:         target.tagName === "TEXTAREA" ||
641:         target.isContentEditable;
642: 
643:       // Inside the Other text field, ←/→ and Home/End move the caret natively.
644:       // ↑/↓ are dual-purpose in the textarea: when the caret has more lines
645:       // to move to in that direction (there's a \n before/after it), let the
646:       // browser handle native caret movement; only steal the keystroke to
647:       // navigate to an adjacent option row when the caret is already at the
648:       // first / last line — otherwise the user can't edit a multi-line draft
649:       // without focus jumping out of the field.
650:       if (isTextInput && e.key !== "ArrowDown" && e.key !== "ArrowUp") return;
651:       if (
652:         isTextInput &&
653:         (e.key === "ArrowUp" || e.key === "ArrowDown") &&
654:         target.tagName === "TEXTAREA"
655:       ) {
656:         // Position-bounds check — works for BOTH explicit `\n` AND visual
657:         // line wraps. Only steal the key when the caret has nowhere left
658:         // to go inside the textarea: ArrowUp at the very start, or
659:         // ArrowDown at the very end. Anywhere else, let the textarea
660:         // handle native caret movement (line-by-line up/down, including
661:         // through wrapped lines without `\n`).
662:         const ta = target as HTMLTextAreaElement;
663:         if (e.key === "ArrowUp" && ta.selectionStart > 0) return;
664:         if (e.key === "ArrowDown" && ta.selectionEnd < ta.value.length) return;
665:       }
666: 
667:       // Our keydown handler and Base UI's RadioGroup composite are merged onto
668:       // the SAME rows container (via the primitive's render prop), and the
669:       // composite's roving focus targets the hidden sr-only radios. Base UI
670:       // runs our (external) handler first and skips its own when we call
671:       // preventBaseUIHandler — without it, every arrow press would land focus
672:       // on an invisible control right after we move it to the next row.
673:       const preventBaseUI = (
674:         e as unknown as { preventBaseUIHandler?: () => void }
675:       ).preventBaseUIHandler;
676: 
677:       if (e.key === "ArrowLeft" || e.key === "ArrowRight") {
678:         e.preventDefault();
679:         e.stopPropagation();
680:         preventBaseUI?.();
681:         if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") {
682:           if (safeIndex > 0) handleBack();
683:         } else if (isSkippable && total > 1) {
684:           handleSkip();
685:         }
686:         return;
687:       }
688: 
689:       if (rowCount === 0) return;
690:       if (
691:         e.key === "ArrowDown" ||
692:         e.key === "ArrowUp" ||
693:         e.key === "Home" ||
694:         e.key === "End"
695:       ) {
696:         e.preventDefault();
697:         e.stopPropagation();
698:         preventBaseUI?.();
699:         let next: number;
700:         if (e.key === "Home") next = 0;
701:         else if (e.key === "End") next = rowCount - 1;
702:         else {
703:           // When focus is in the Other field, treat it as the Other row.
704:           const base = isTextInput ? otherIndex : activeIndex ?? -1;
705:           next = e.key === "ArrowDown" ? base + 1 : base - 1;
706:           next = (next + rowCount) % rowCount;
707:         }
708:         moveActive(next);
709:       }
710:     };

712:     // Cmd+Enter (macOS) / Ctrl+Enter (Windows/Linux) commits a multi-select
713:     // question, mirroring the Continue button. Handled at the root so it works
714:     // wherever focus sits inside the card, and scoped to this instance because
715:     // the event has to bubble up from a focused descendant (no global listener,
716:     // so stacked demos don't all fire at once).

718:       if (e.key !== "Enter") return;

722:       if (!mod || !(isMulti || isFreeText)) return;

724:       if (isFreeText) {
725:         if (otherText.trim().length > 0) handleOtherSubmit();

727:       }

732:     if (!question) {
733:       return (
734:         <div
735:           ref={ref}
736:           className={cn(
737:             "w-full max-w-[520px] p-5 bg-card border border-border",
738:             shape.container,

748:     // ── Layout calculations for hover/focus indicators ───────────
749:     // focusedIndex comes from the rows container's onFocus (see rowsContent),
750:     // set only when the focused row matches :focus-visible — so the blue
751:     // morphing ring tracks keyboard focus across option rows. It is
752:     // intentionally suppressed for the Other field: that row has its own
753:     // input-field treatment (the "type here" hint when empty, the merged
754:     // selected bg once it has text), so the ring is redundant there and reads
755:     // as noise while typing. focusedIndex is still tracked for the hint and
756:     // submit-arrow visibility — we just don't draw a ring around it.
757:     const focusRect =
758:       focusedIndex !== null && !(allowOther && focusedIndex === otherIndex)
759:         ? itemRects[focusedIndex]

762:     // ── Selected-row grouping (merges contiguous selections) ─────
763:     // Mirrors the CheckboxGroup pattern: contiguous selected indices
764:     // collapse into a single rounded background block; stable IDs let
765:     // framer-motion morph block size/position when neighbours toggle.
766:     // The Other row gets its own input-field-style indicator (see below) and
767:     // is intentionally excluded here so it doesn't merge into a contiguous
768:     // bg-accent block with adjacent selected options.
769:     // Include the Other row in selectedIndices when it has text. This lets
770:     // it merge into the same morphing bg block as adjacent selected options
771:     // (instead of looking like a disconnected input field next to them).
772:     const selectedIndices = useMemo(() => {
773:       const set = new Set<number>();
774:       options.forEach((opt, i) => {
775:         if (selectedIds.includes(optionKey(opt, i))) set.add(i);
776:       });
777:       if (allowOther && otherText.length > 0) set.add(otherIndex);
778:       return set;
779:     }, [options, selectedIds, allowOther, otherText, otherIndex]);
780: 
781:     const selectedGroups = useMemo(() => {
782:       const runs: { start: number; end: number }[] = [];
783:       const sorted = [...selectedIndices].sort((a, b) => a - b);
784:       for (const idx of sorted) {
785:         const last = runs[runs.length - 1];
786:         if (last && idx === last.end + 1) last.end = idx;
787:         else runs.push({ start: idx, end: idx });
788:       }
789: 
790:       // Stable run IDs so a growing/shrinking run animates instead of
791:       // exit+re-enter when neighbours flip.
792:       const usedIds = new Set<number>();
793:       const nextGroupMap = new Map<number, number>();
794:       const groups = runs.map((run) => {
795:         let stableId: number | null = null;
796:         for (let i = run.start; i <= run.end; i++) {
797:           const prev = prevGroupMapRef.current.get(i);
798:           if (prev !== undefined && !usedIds.has(prev)) {
799:             stableId = prev;
800:             break;
801:           }
802:         }
803:         const id = stableId ?? ++groupIdCounterRef.current;
804:         usedIds.add(id);
805:         for (let i = run.start; i <= run.end; i++) nextGroupMap.set(i, id);
806:         return { ...run, id };
807:       });
808:       prevGroupMapRef.current = nextGroupMap;
809:       return groups;
810:     }, [selectedIndices]);

812:     // Selected backgrounds, with the merge/split boundary animation when one
813:     // unselected row bridges or splits two selected runs. Selected backgrounds
814:     // use shape.bg, so corners animate around its radius.
815:     const blocks = useMergeSplitBlocks(selectedGroups, itemRects, shape.bgRadius);
816: 
817:     const showBack = total > 1 && safeIndex > 0;
818:     const showSkip = total > 1 && isSkippable;
819:     // freeText commits through the same bottom submit button as multi-select.
820:     const showSubmit = isMulti || isFreeText;
821:     const showFooter = showBack || showSkip || showSubmit;

823:     // ── Roving tabindex ──────────────────────────────────────────
824:     // One tab stop for the whole group, single- AND multi-select alike: the
825:     // first selected row, or — when the question is unanswered — the first
826:     // row, so the group stays keyboard-reachable (the hasSelection-style
827:     // fallback from registry/base). Arrows handle row-to-row movement; Tab
828:     // moves on past the group. The Other row never takes the stop — its
829:     // textarea is natively focusable on its own.
830:     const firstSelectedRow = options.findIndex((opt, i) =>
831:       selectedIds.includes(optionKey(opt, i))
832:     );

834:     // ── Option rows ──────────────────────────────────────────────
835:     // The rows container is handed to a Base UI group primitive via `render`
836:     // (Radio.Group for single-select, Checkbox.Group for multi-select — see
837:     // the JSX below), so group semantics and selection plumbing come from
838:     // Base UI while the rows keep their custom fluid-hover treatment.
839:     // Each option Row hosts a hidden sr-only Radio/Checkbox primitive; the
840:     // visible wrapper carries role/aria-checked. CAUTION: every keyboard-nav
841:     // query in here is scoped to [data-fluid-hover-index] — a bare
842:     // [role="radio"] / [role="checkbox"] selector would ALSO match the hidden
843:     // primitive inside each row (two hits per row) and land arrow-key focus
844:     // on invisible controls.
845:     const rowsContent = (
846:       <div
847:         ref={rowsContainerRef}
848:         role={isMulti ? "group" : "radiogroup"}
849:         aria-labelledby={`${reactId}-${qId}-title`}
850:         onMouseEnter={handlers.onMouseEnter}
851:         onMouseMove={handlers.onMouseMove}
852:         onMouseLeave={handlers.onMouseLeave}
853:         onClick={handlers.onClick}
854:         onFocus={(e) => {
855:           // Track focus at the container (React's onFocus is focusin, so row
856:           // and Other-textarea focus both bubble here). activeIndex mirrors

12: function toMemoryEntry(memory: Memory): MemoryEntry {
13: 	const metadata = (memory.metadata ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
14: 	const category = metadata.category as MemoryCategory | undefined;
15: 	return {
16: 		id: memory.id,
17: 		text: memory.memory ?? "",
18: 		category: memoryCategorySchema.safeParse(category).success
19: 			? (category as MemoryCategory)
20: 			: "semantic",
21: 		createdAt: memory.createdAt?.toISOString() ?? new Date().toISOString(),
22: 		score: memory.score,
23: 		metadata,
24: 	};
25: }
26: 
27: /**
28:  * Mem0-hosted memory backend. Ownership is enforced through the exact mem0
29:  * user id: every store/search/list is scoped to the workflow owner's id, so no
30:  * memory can ever leak across users.
31:  *
32:  * When no API key is configured the store degrades to a null backend: store
33:  * succeeds silently and search/list return nothing, so an undeployed memory
34:  * integration never breaks an execution.
35:  */
36: export class Mem0MemoryStore implements MemoryStore {
37: 	private readonly client: MemoryClient | null;
38: 
39: 	constructor(apiKey: string) {
40: 		this.client = apiKey ? new MemoryClient({ apiKey }) : null;
41: 	}
42: 
43: 	async store(input: StoreMemoryInput): Promise<{ id: string }> {
44: 		if (!this.client) {
45: 			return { id: "mem_offline" };
46: 		}
47: 		const results = await this.client.add(
48: 			[{ role: "user", content: input.text }],
49: 			{
50: 				userId: input.userId,
51: 				infer: false,
52: 				metadata: {
53: 					category: input.category ?? "semantic",
54: 					workflowId: input.workflowId,
55: 					executionId: input.executionId,
56: 					...input.metadata,
57: 				},
58: 			},
59: 		);
60: 		const memory = results[0];
61: 		return { id: memory?.id ?? "mem_ok" };
62: 	}
63: 
64: 	async search(input: SearchMemoryInput): Promise<MemoryEntry[]> {
65: 		if (!this.client) {
66: 			return [];
67: 		}
68: 		const allowed = input.categories
69: 			? new Set<MemoryCategory>(input.categories)
70: 			: null;
71: 		const { results } = await this.client.search(input.query, {
72: 			filters: { user_id: input.userId },
73: 			topK: input.limit ?? 5,
74: 			threshold: input.threshold,
75: 		});
76: 		return results
77: 			.map(toMemoryEntry)
78: 			.filter((entry) => !allowed || allowed.has(entry.category))
79: 			.slice(0, input.limit ?? 5);
80: 	}
81: 
82: 	async listForUser(input: {
83: 		userId: string;
84: 		limit?: number;
85: 	}): Promise<MemoryEntry[]> {
86: 		if (!this.client) {
87: 			return [];
88: 		}
89: 		const { results } = await this.client.getAll({
90: 			filters: { user_id: input.userId },
91: 			page: 1,
92: 			pageSize: input.limit ?? 20,
93: 		});
94: 		return results.map(toMemoryEntry).slice(0, input.limit ?? 20);
95: 	}
96: 
97: 	async deleteByIds(userId: string, ids: string[]): Promise<void> {
98: 		if (!this.client || ids.length === 0) {
99: 			return;
100: 		}
101: 		const owned = new Set(
102: 			(await this.listForUser({ userId, limit: 200 })).map((entry) => entry.id),
103: 		);
104: 		for (const id of ids) {
105: 			if (!owned.has(id)) {
106: 				continue;
107: 			}
108: 			try {
109: 				await this.client.delete(id);
110: 			} catch {
111: 				// A missing/already-deleted memory is a no-op, never a hard error.
112: 			}
113: 		}
114: 	}
115: 
116: 	async deleteAllForUser(userId: string): Promise<void> {
117: 		if (!this.client) {
118: 			return;
119: 		}
120: 		await this.client.deleteAll({ userId });
121: 	}
122: }

# Aevryn — Code Review Observations

Audited: monorepo at `D:\github-desktop\aevryn` (read-only).
Scope: whole repo described in `AGENTS.md`, `internal/` decisions/plans, all
`NEWTODO` markers, and the live data paths they depend on.

---

## 1. What the system is today

A persistent web-agent platform. The legacy flow:

```
Next.js UI (hardcoded demo)
→ tRPC router  packages/api/src/routers/agent.ts  (630 lines)
→ WorkflowService  packages/workflow/src/services/workflow-service.ts  (1517 lines)
→ 13 repositories → Drizzle → PostgreSQL
   +  Inngest functions:
       execution-run.ts (914 lines)   — the whole agent loop
       schedule-tick.ts  (143 lines)  — cron + sleep/wake
       notification-notifier.ts       — webhook delivery
```

Capabilities (`packages/agent`): 13 registered capabilities wrapping 6 Anakin
adapters (search/scrape/crawl/map/research/wire) + browser sessions + memory +
schedules. Approval-gated: `wireAction`, `browserSessionCreate/Rename/Delete`.

LLM (Groq via Vercel AI SDK `ai` v7): `runAgent` in
`packages/agent/src/runtime.ts` drives a single `generateText` loop with
`isStepCount(maxSteps)` and the SDK's `toolApproval` gate. Plans and runtime
decisions are extracted from the model's final text with `/\`\`\`json...\`\`\`/`
regex in `packages/inngest/src/functions/execution-run.ts:48`.

Re-architecture already decided in `internal/plans/2026-09-10-aevryn-rearchitecture/`
and `internal/ALL-DECISIONS.md`:
thread === workflow, first message ≠ objective, planning output =
`AskUserQuestion[]` (MCQ), chat streams in the web app via `POST /api/chat`
(`useChat` + zod tools `askUserQuestion` / `showPlan` / `finalizeAndInject`),
ONE Inngest `execution/run` event only on plan approval, Supabase Auth,
mem0 per-thread memory. `apps/web/src/app/workspace/[threadId]/page.tsx` is the
empty stub that must become this.

---

## 2. NEWTODO inventory (the user's own work order)

| # | File:line | Ask |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `packages/auth/README.md:1` | Rebuild auth — Supabase Google signup ONLY |
| 2 | `packages/api/README.md:1` | Rebuild API ("only when 100% sure") |
| 3 | `packages/agent/src/README.md:1` | Fix `runtime.ts` hardcoded prompts → real prompt library module |
| 4 | `packages/agent/src/adapters/README.md:1,3` | Decide how adapter schemas reach the LLM (tool call vs global memory); note: schemas already live in capabilities via `inputSchema` |
| 5 | `packages/agent/src/adapters/scrape.ts:1` | Verify exact `@anakin-io/sdk` `ScrapeFormat` list (current union may be wrong) |
| 6 | `packages/workflow/README.md:1` | Rebuild `workflow` package after new plan |
| 7 | `packages/db/src/schema/README.md:1,3` | Migrate current schema first, then design a brand-new schema |
| 8 | `packages/inngest/src/README.md:1,3` | Inngest only for thread-bound workflow event + cron; rebuild `/inngest` (functions dir too big) |
| 9 | `packages/ui/src/components/ui/ask-user-questions.tsx:37` | `AskUserQuestion` interface WILL be the schema the LLM gets via tool call |
| 10 | `packages/ui/src/components/header/searchable-dropdown.tsx:16,41` | Real workflows/groups from DB; unify the header input bar into one place |
| 11 | `packages/ui/src/components/sidebar-preset/nav-data.ts:18` | Real data from DB |
| 12 | `apps/web/src/app/workspace/page.tsx:253` | Run button visible only after workflow planned + approved + bound |
| 13 | `apps/web/src/app/workspace/page.tsx:338` | `mb-40` spacing → new component or inline utility |

---

## 3. Confirmed breakages (behind "cron not working", "AI SDK not working")

1. **`schedule-tick` has no trigger and is never served.**
   `packages/inngest/src/functions/schedule-tick.ts:21-25` declares
   `inngest.createFunction({ id: "schedule-tick", retries: 2 }, ...)` with no
   `triggers` array, and `apps/web/src/app/api/inngest/route.ts:9` registers
   ONLY `executionRun`. Result: cron jobs, sleep→wake, and due-work sweeping
   can never fire. This is the root cause of "cron broken".

2. **`notificationNotifier` is also never served.** `notification/publish`
   events (`execution-run.ts:763`) are dropped at the SDK boundary → webhook
   notifications and anywhere-outside-the-app delivery are dead.

3. **`resumeWorkflow` does nothing useful.**
   `workflow-service.ts:1024` flips `paused → active` but never enqueues a new
   execution or sends `execution/run`. A "resumed" workflow sits idle forever.

4. **Orphaned executions on event-send failure.** Every mutator in
   `agent.ts` (`sendMessage`, `confirmWorkflow`, `updateObjective`,
   `runWorkflow`, `resolveApproval`) follows
   `enqueueMessage() → inngest.send()` and on send error calls
   `failExecution()`, but the row created by `enqueueMessage` stays
   `pending`. If `inngest.send` throws after enqueue, nothing ever processes
   that execution → permanent orphan. This send+fail block is copy-pasted 5×
   and is the prime candidate to kill when `/api/chat` takes over.

5. **Decision parsing is regex over free-text.** `extractPlan`/`extractDecision`
   (`execution-run.ts:48`) parse a fenced ```json block out of the model's
   final message. Fragile by design and contradicts AGENTS.md rule 8/9/10
   (structured schemas, no free-text control). The re-architecture replaces it
   with real SDK tool calls. Same for `planning.ts:21` (JSON-in-prose).

6. **Cost budget is post-hoc, not bound.** `runAgentStep` checks
   `result.usage.costUsd > EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD` AFTER the whole run completes
   (`execution-run.ts:594`). It can never stop a run from overspending, it only
   schedules a recovery afterwards.

7. **`replayedToolOutputs` is keyed by tool name** (`runtime.ts:160`) and
   consumed once. Fine for the single-retry case, but two capabilities with the
   same name would collide; also replay happens before the response cap, so a
   huge persisted output can refill context.

8. **`GROQ_MODEL` default is `openai/gpt-oss-20b`** (`packages/env/src/server.ts:35`).
   Verify this exact model id exists on Groq — if the dev was running a local
   override this default may 404 in production. `MEM0_API_KEY` defaults to `""`
   (silent no-op backend).

9. **`resumeWorkflow` + pause semantics.** `pauseWorkflow` cancels live
   executions (`workflow-service.ts:985`) and flips workflow to "paused";
   schedules are NOT disabled on pause (they just no-op while paused). See #3.

10. **No `/api/chat`, no realtime.** The workspace renders a fully hardcoded
    conversation (`workspace/page.tsx`, 567 lines: mock `questions`,
    `workflowApproval`, accordion plan, tool-step cards, table). `trpc` client
    exists (`apps/web/src/utils/trpc.ts`) but nothing in workspace calls it.
    `[threadId]/page.tsx` is 8 lines of stub.

---

## 4. Architecture / data-model observations

- **`WorkflowService` is a 66-public-method god class** spanning every domain
  concept (workflow, execution, steps, state, schedule, approval, notification,
  observation, recovery, webhook, usage). The `internal/02-BACKEND-AUDIT.md`
  split is still correct; do not rebuild the same shape.
- **Bad JSONB typing:** `notification.body` and `recoveryAttempt.detail` are
  `$type<z.input<typeof eventDataSchema>>` (`notification.ts:29`,
  `recovery-attempt.ts:36`) — a domain model forced onto the event data schema.
  Harmless at runtime, misleading to readers, and the new schema should drop it.
- **IDs:** domain tables use `text("id")` PKs and `@aevryn/db` `ids.*` /
  `isValidId`. Verify every new table gets a prefixed ULID and that
  `ID_PREFIXES` in `packages/db/src/ids.ts` stays in sync with the AGENTS.md
  prefix list (wf_/exe_/step_/tool_/mem_/evt_/rec_).
- **Auth tables keep OAuth tokens in plaintext** (`account.access_token`/`refresh_token`,
  `auth.ts:52-53`). Standard better-auth shape, but silently conflicts with
  "never store secrets" — will be deleted anyway by the Supabase Auth rebuild.
- **Memory:** only `Mem0MemoryStore` implements `MemoryStore`
  (`memory/mem0-store.ts`). It degrades silently without a key. AGENTS.md and
  `internal/08` target PostgreSQL + pgvector with a deliberate write policy;
  mem0 is hosted and per `userId`, which also fights the "adapter schemas as
  GLOBAL memory" idea in `adapters/README.md:1` (mem0 scopes by user, so a
  schema memory would not be global). Decide and document; current state is
  both.
- **Good parts worth keeping:** optimistic-concurrency `applyState` (version
  checks), `webhookBoard` token hashing, idempotent `resolveExecutionState`
  gate, bounded recovery with `recordRecoveryAttempt` returning a boolean so
  concurrent failure handlers cannot double-schedule, `replayedToolOutputs`
  honoring the "never re-run a possibly-succeeded side effect" rule, Evlog
  instrumentation + request-id plumbing (`proxy.ts`, `evlog.ts`), and the
  `ask-user-questions.tsx` component itself (the exact UX the new tool schema
  must feed).
- **UI stack is ready** but unwired: `QueryClientProvider` is active
  (`providers.tsx:41`), zustand is installed with zero stores, and every data
  surface (sidebar nav, dropdown, workspace) is mocked.

---

## 5. Suggested work order (aligned with the user's NEWTODOs)

1. Fix triggers/services first: give `schedule-tick` a real cron trigger (or
   move cron to a DB-driven sweeper invoked by Inngest `cron`), and register
   `notificationNotifier` in `apps/web/src/app/api/inngest/route.ts`.
2. Supabase Auth rebuild (`packages/auth`) — GIANT prerequisite for every
   `ctx.session` and the whole UI.
3. Schema: run `db:generate`/`db:migrate` NOW to snapshot the current schema
   (NEWTODO #7) before redesigning tables for the new thread/chat model.
4. `/api/chat` route + `useChat` + zod tools (`askUserQuestion`, `showPlan`,
   `finalizeAndInject`); derive the `AskUserQuestion` zod schema directly from
   the component interface (`ask-user-questions.tsx:38`).
5. Inngest shrink to exactly: thread-bound `execution/run` (send only on
   approval) + cron; delete the regex plan/decision extraction and the 5×
   duplicated send/fail blocks.
6. Wire UI: `searchable-dropdown`, `nav-data`, workspace page, per-thread
   routing, realtime via chat streaming; keep `run` button gated on bound/
   approved state (NEWTODO #12).
7. Sweep the ScrapeFormat union against the installed `@anakin-io/sdk`
   (`scrape.ts:1`) and set `GROQ_MODEL` to a confirmed live model id.

All findings are verifiable by reading the cited files; none of this is a code
change — this file documents the state as of the audit.

**`@anakin-io/sdk` `0.1.0`** — alpha (v0.1.x), Apache-2.0, Node >= 18, dual ESM+CJS (~28 KB).

- tgz filename + `package.json` version: `0.1.0`
- `VERSION` export const: `"0.1.0"`
- Repo pin: `packages/agent/package.json` → `"@anakin-io/sdk": "^0.1.0"`

---

## (b) Complete SDK v0.1.0 surface (from `index.d.ts`, export list)

### Client methods (`class Anakin`)
| Method | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scrape` | `(url, options?: ScrapeOptions) => Promise<Document>` | Single URL → markdown/html/cleanedHtml/links/images/summary/screenshot/json. Polls internally. |
| `map` | `(url, options?: MapOptions) => Promise<MapResult>` | URL discovery on a domain (links, depth, external). |
| `crawl` | `(url, options?: CrawlOptions) => Promise<CrawlResult>` | Bulk-fetch up to N pages of a site, pattern-filtered, per-page markdown/html. |
| `search` | `(prompt, options?: SearchOptions) => Promise<SearchResult>` | AI web search w/ citations. **Synchronous** (no polling). |
| `agenticSearch` | `(prompt, options?: AgenticSearchOptions) => Promise<AgenticSearchResult>` | Multi-source deep research, 1–5 min, optional output schema, `useBrowser`. |
| `wire` | `(actionId, params, options?: WireOptions) => Promise<WireResult>` | Execute pre-built website action (940+ sites) — login flows, form submissions, read-only extracts. |
| `countries` | `() => Country[]` | Static bundled country list — no network call. |
| `sessions` | `SessionsClient` instance | Browser-session CRUD (authenticated scraping). |

### `SessionsClient` methods
| Method | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | `(options?: { domain? }) => Promise<BrowserSession[]>` | List saved sessions, optional domain filter. |
| `create` | `(options: { websiteUrl, name, record?, sessionType? }) => Promise<BrowserSessionHandle>` | Spawn interactive browser (noVNC URL, access token, WS URL) for manual login. |
| `save` | `(browserInstanceId: string) => Promise<BrowserSession>` | Persist the interactive browser's cookies+localStorage as a session. |
| `update` | `(sessionId, { name }) => Promise<BrowserSession>` | Rename session. |
| `delete` | `(sessionId) => Promise<void>` | Permanently delete session storage. |

### Tool/config types
- `AnakinClientOptions`: `apiKey`, `baseUrl`, `timeoutMs`, `maxRetries`, `pollIntervalMs`, `pollMaxIntervalMs`, `pollTimeoutMs` (env fallback `ANAKIN_API_KEY`)
- `ScrapeOptions`: `formats`, `country`, `useBrowser`, `generateJson`, `forceFresh`, `sessionId`, `sessionName`, `pollTimeoutMs`
- `MapOptions`: `limit`, `depth`, `limitPerLevel`, `includeSubdomains`, `includeExternalLinks`, `search`, `useBrowser`, `sessionId`, `pollTimeoutMs`
- `CrawlOptions`: `maxPages`, `depth`, `includePatterns` (glob), `excludePatterns`, `country`, `useBrowser`, `sessionId`, `pollTimeoutMs`
- `SearchOptions`: `limit`
- `AgenticSearchOptions`: `useBrowser`, `schema` (JSON Schema → controls extracted shape), `pollTimeoutMs`
- `WireOptions`: `pollTimeoutMs`
- `SessionsListOptions`: `domain`; `SessionsCreateOptions`: `websiteUrl`, `name`, `record`, `sessionType`
- `HttpClientOptions`/`PollOptions` (internal): baseUrl/timeout/maxRetries; poll with `isTerminal`, backoff ×1.5 capped, wall-clock timeout

### Result types
- `Document`: `id, url, status, cached, durationMs, createdAt?, completedAt?, markdown?, html?, cleanedHtml?, links?, images?, summary?, generatedJson?, screenshotUrl?, fullPageScreenshotUrl?, error?`
- `MapResult`: `id, url, links[], totalLinks, externalLinks[], totalExternalLinks, durationMs`
- `CrawlResult`: `id, url, totalPages, completedPages, pages[], durationMs`; `CrawlPage`: `url, status, markdown?, html?, durationMs, error?`
- `SearchResult`: `id, results[]`; `SearchResultItem`: `url, title?, snippet?, date?, lastUpdated?`
- `AgenticSearchResult`: `id, status, jobType, generatedJson?{ summary?, structured_data?, data_schema? }, cached, createdAt?, completedAt?, durationMs, error?`
- `WireResult`: `jobId, status, data?, creditsUsed, executionMs, error?{code,message}`
- `BrowserSession`: `id, name?, websiteUrl?, websiteDomain?, isActive, createdAt?, lastUsedAt?, expiresAt?, cookieCount?, storageItemCount?`
- `BrowserSessionHandle`: `sessionId, novncUrl?, accessToken?, expiresIn?, wsUrl?`
- `TerminalStatus`: `'completed' | 'failed'`; `Country`: `{ code, name? }`

### Error hierarchy (all extend `AnakinError`: `statusCode?, requestId?, code?, body?`)
`ConfigurationError`, `AuthenticationError`, `WireAuthRequiredError` (extends Authentication, has `.connectUrl` — fires on Wire 401 `AUTH_REQUIRED`), `ForbiddenError`, `NotFoundError`, `InvalidRequestError`, `InsufficientCreditsError` (`.balance`, `.required`), `RateLimitError` (`.retryAfter`), `ServerError`, `JobFailedError`, `JobTimeoutError`, `NetworkError`.

### Constants
`SUPPORTED_COUNTRIES` (readonly Country[]), `SUPPORTED_COUNTRY_CODES` (ReadonlySet, e.g. `.has("us")`), `VERSION = "0.1.0"`.

---

## (c) ScrapeFormat exact enum

```ts
type ScrapeFormat =
  | 'markdown'
  | 'html'
  | 'cleanedHtml'
  | 'json'
  | 'links'
  | 'images'

Docs confirm (line 5321): default = markdown + html + cleanedHtml; `screenshot`/`screenshotFullPage` auto-enable headless browser and return API-key-authed `screenshotUrl` / `fullPageScreenshotUrl` pointing at `GET /v1/url-scraper/{id}/screenshot` (streams raw PNG; repo would need to fetch with `X-API-Key` — SDK does NOT wrap the download).

---

## (d) What adapters use today

| Adapter | SDK methods called | Options forwarded |
|---|---|---|
| `anakin-scrape` | `client.scrape` | formats, country, useBrowser, generateJson, forceFresh, sessionId, sessionName |
| `anakin-search` | `client.search` | limit |
| `anakin-crawl` | `client.crawl` | maxPages, depth, includePatterns, excludePatterns, country, useBrowser, sessionId |

| `anakin-research` | `client.agenticSearch` | useBrowser, schema |
| `anakin-wire` | `client.wire` | — (actionId + params) |
| `anakin-browser-session` | `sessions.list` / `create` / `update` / `delete` | domain; websiteUrl/name/record/sessionType; rename; delete |

Also used: **error hierarchy** in `errors.ts` — every class imported (AnakinError base → `ANAKIN_ERROR`, RateLimit→retryable, ServerError/NetworkError/JobTimeout→retryable, WireAuthRequired/JobFailed/NotFound→recoverable, rest fatal) + `provider.requestId`/`error.code` surfaced. `registry.ts` wires all 7 adapters. **Nothing called:** `sessions.save`, `countries()`, `SUPPORTED_COUNTRIES/CODES`, `VERSION`, `AnakinClientOptions` polling knobs (defaults used).

---

## (e) Unused-but-available capabilities

**In the SDK, not exercised by repo:**
1. `sessions.save(browserInstanceId)` — programmatic session save (adapters cover create/list/update/delete only). Enables the full interactive-login→save→authenticated-scrape loop.
2. Screenshot pipeline — `formats: ['screenshot','screenshotFullPage']` + `screenshotUrl`/`fullPageScreenshotUrl` in `Document` (adapter passes fields through, but nothing requests them). Raw PNG download needs manual authed GET — SDK doesn't wrap it.
3. `ScrapeFormat` surface not used: `'json'`, `'links'`, `'images'`, `'summary'`, `'cleanedHtml'`, `'html'` (adapter accepts, no caller asks).
4. `forceFresh: true` — bypass cache (30x cache speedup is default; forceFresh for stale pages).
5. `countries()` + `SUPPORTED_COUNTRIES`/`SUPPORTED_COUNTRY_CODES` — validation/autocomplete bundled free.
6. `generateJson` w/ structured extraction on plain scrape (adapter passes it, repo never sets it).
7. Polling tuning (`pollTimeoutMs` per-call, `pollIntervalMs/maxIntervalMs/timeoutMs/maxRetries` per-client) — Wire's `creditsUsed`/`executionMs`, `Document.cached`, `AgenticSearchResult.jobType` diagnostics already passed through but unused by callers.

**REST-only capabilities (in llms-full/API docs, NOT in SDK v0.1.0 — reachable only via raw HTTP or future SDK versions):**
8. **Batch scraping** — `POST /v1/url-scraper/batch`, up to 10 URLs/job; per-URL child job IDs whose screenshots are fetched individually.
9. **Inline scrape** — `POST /v1/url-scraper/scrape` (200 inline / 202 poll same read).
10. **`outputSchema`** on scrape (JSON Schema → `generatedJson`; implies `generateJson`) — SDK only exposes `schema` on agenticSearch.
11. **Monitoring** — `/v1/monitors` CRUD, `POST /monitors/{id}/pause|resume|run-now`, snapshots/changes, `watchMode: full_page|specific_data|wire`, webhook/email alerts, min interval 15 min. Zero SDK support.
12. **AI Visibility** — `POST /v1/ai-visibility/search` fans prompt to ChatGPT+Gemini+Google AI Overview; poll `search/{id}`, list searches, retry source, list sources, `country` geo. Zero SDK support.
13. **Webhooks** — per-request `webhook_url` on any async submit (`job.completed/failed`, `batch.*`, `wire.job.*`, `monitor.change`, `ai.search.*`) + signed HMAC-SHA256 deliveries (`X-Anakin-Signature`), endpoint management, delivery log/resend, signing-secret rotate. SDK has no webhook helpers.
14. **Wire extras** — discovery (`GET /v1/wire/catalog`, `/{slug}`, `/resolve` or `/search`), identities (`/identities`, `/login` = create-id+sign-in, `/credentials/verify` re-login), identity sources/vaults (1Password, Azure Key Vault: connect/list/rotate/verify/disconnect + containers/entries browse), `POST /v1/wire/build-request` (generate new action), `POST /v1/wire-run` (Zero Touch, keyless read-only sync), and **file-producing actions** (`data: null` + `files[]` manifest, download bytes via `GET /wire/jobs/{id}/download` — e.g. PDFs). SDK wraps only `wire(actionId, params)`.
15. **Browser API** (CDP WebSocket) — `wss://api.anakin.io/v1/browser-connect` with `X-API-Key`; full Playwright/Puppeteer control NOT in the SDK: navigate (`goto`, tokens: domcontentloaded/load), **click, fill/type, keyboard, mouse, drag, scroll/pagination, select, waits** (`wait_for_selector`/`waitForSelector`, `wait_for_function`, `waitForNavigation`), `evaluate`, `locator`/`$$`/`$eval`, `screenshot`, **multi-tab** (`context.newPage()`, `browser.newPage()`), request/response/console/websocket/pageerror events, `route()`/`unroute()` interception, `set_extra_http_headers`, geo `?country=GB`, `?save_session=`/`?session_id=`/`?session_name=`, `?record=true` WebM recording, `?api_key=` query auth. Selenium unsupported.
16. **Browser sessions REST** — `GET /v1/sessions?domain=`, `PATCH /v1/sessions/:id` rename, `DELETE /v1/sessions/:id` (SDK covers these; mirror also available raw).
17. **Countries endpoint** — `GET /v1/countries` live list (SDK ships static copy instead).
18. **Session-in-browser reuse** — `sessionId`/`sessionName` already forwarded by 4 adapters, so authenticated scraping works; but the *save* step (cap #1) plus interactive noVNC handle (`novncUrl`, `wsUrl` in `BrowserSessionHandle`) are unexercised — no human-in-the-loop login flow exists in the repo.

**Node vs browser API difference (headline):** the packaged SDK is **Node-only** (built-in fetch; ESM+CJS; no browser build) and does **not** do browser automation — click/type/drag/scroll/tabs/downloads/waits/cookies all live in the separate CDP **Browser API** (`wss://api.anakin.io/v1/browser-connect`), driven by your own Playwright/Puppeteer. Sessions bridge both: created/saved via SDK, but connectable raw via `?session_id=` on the WS, and re-usable on scrapes via `sessionId`/`sessionName`.

# Skill: ai-sdk

## What the AI SDK Is

The AI SDK by Vercel (the `ai` package on npm) is a TypeScript toolkit for building AI applications. It provides a unified API across model providers for text generation, structured output, tool calling, agents, embeddings, and framework UI integrations.

- Repository: https://github.com/vercel/ai
- Documentation: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs

## Critical: Do Not Trust Your Own Memory

Whatever you remember about the AI SDK is likely outdated. The SDK changes frequently across versions - APIs are renamed, removed, and added. Your training data almost certainly contains obsolete APIs, deprecated patterns, and model IDs that no longer exist. UI hooks like `useChat` are among the most frequently changed APIs, so be especially careful with client code.

**Never write AI SDK code from memory.** Always verify every API, option, and pattern against the documentation and source code for the version that is actually installed in the project.

## Use the Bundled, Version-Matched Docs

The `ai` package ships its full documentation and source code inside `node_modules`. These always match the installed version, so trust them over anything you remember.

1. Ensure `ai` is installed. If `node_modules/ai/` does not exist, install **only** the `ai` package using the project's package manager (e.g. `pnpm add ai`). Install provider packages (e.g. `@ai-sdk/openai`) and framework packages (e.g. `@ai-sdk/react`) later, when the task requires them.
2. Read and grep the bundled docs at `node_modules/ai/docs/` and the source at `node_modules/ai/src/`.
3. Provider and framework packages bundle their own docs at `node_modules/@ai-sdk/<name>/docs/`.
4. If something isn't in the bundled docs, search https://ai-sdk.dev/docs. You can append `.md` to any docs page URL to get its markdown, and search via `https://ai-sdk.dev/api/search-docs?q=your_query`.
5. If you cannot find support for an answer in the docs or source, say so explicitly — do not guess.

## AI Gateway: The Fastest Way to Start

The Vercel AI Gateway is the fastest way to get started with the AI SDK. It provides access to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other providers through a single API, without installing provider packages or managing multiple API keys.

To set it up:

1. Authenticate with OIDC (for Vercel deployments) or get an AI Gateway API key.
2. Provide it to your app via the `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` environment variable.
3. Reference models with `provider/model` strings.

For exact setup, authentication, and usage, read the bundled guide and the AI Gateway docs.

### Choosing a Model

Never use model IDs from memory — models are released and retired frequently. Fetch the current list before writing code that references a model. Do not truncate the list (e.g. with `head`) so you can find the newest models:

```bash
# All available models
curl -s https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models | jq -r '.data[].id'

# Filter by provider (e.g. anthropic, openai, google)
curl -s https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.id | startswith("anthropic/")) | .id] | reverse | .[]'
```

When multiple versions of a model exist, prefer the one with the highest version number.

## Building and Consuming Agents

Use the SDK's built-in agent abstraction (such as `ToolLoopAgent`) rather than hand-rolling tool-calling loops. For end-to-end type safety, infer the UI message type from your agent definition when consuming it on the client (e.g. with `useChat`). Consuming an agent is framework-specific: check `package.json` to detect the stack, then follow the matching quickstart.

Look up the current agent, tool, and type-safety APIs in the bundled docs (`node_modules/ai/docs/`, especially the agents section) or at https://ai-sdk.dev/docs.

## DevTools

AI SDK DevTools captures your AI SDK calls - requests, responses, tool calls, token usage, and multi-step runs - so you can inspect exactly what your agents do. Use it while developing to debug generations. It is a separate package and is intended for local development only.

For setup instructions, read the bundled DevTools documentation.

## Keep the SDK Current

Outdated installs are the most common source of errors. Compare the installed version against the latest:

- **Installed:** the `version` field in `node_modules/ai/package.json`.
- **Latest:** run `npm view ai version`.

If the installed version is a major version (or more) behind the latest, tell the user they are on an old release, and recommend upgrading before continuing. Migration guides are at https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/migration-guides.

## After Making Changes

Run the project's type checker. Be minimal — only set options that differ from the defaults, checking docs or source for the defaults rather than over-specifying. Most type errors come from remembered, now-changed APIs; re-check the current docs and source when they occur.

# Skill: supabase

# Supabase

## Core Principles

**1. Supabase changes frequently — verify against changelog and current docs before implementing.**
Do not rely on training data for Supabase features. Function signatures, config.toml settings, and API conventions change between versions.

First, fetch `https://supabase.com/changelog.md` (a lightweight summary index — not a heavy pull), scan for `breaking-change` tags relevant to your task, and follow the linked page for any that apply. Then look up the relevant topic using the documentation access methods below.

**2. Verify your work.**
After implementing any fix, run a test query to confirm the change works. A fix without verification is incomplete.

**3. Recover from errors, don't loop.**
If an approach fails after 2-3 attempts, stop and reconsider. Try a different method, check documentation, inspect the error more carefully, and review relevant logs when available. Supabase issues are not always solved by retrying the same command, and the answer is not always in the logs, but logs are often worth checking before proceeding.

**4. Exposing tables to the Data API:** Depending on the user's [Data API settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/<ref>/integrations/data_api/settings), newly created tables may not be automatically exposed via the Data (REST) API. If this is the case, `anon` and `authenticated` roles will need to be explicitly granted access.

> Note that this is separate from RLS, which controls which _rows_ are visible once a table is accessible, not whether the table is accessible at all.

When a user reports a SQL-created table is unexpectedly inaccessible, check their Data API settings and whether the roles have been granted access via explicit `GRANT` SQL. When granting public (`anon`/`authenticated`) access, always enable RLS too. See [Exposing a Table to the Data API](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api.md) for the full setup workflow.

**5. RLS in exposed schemas.**
Enable RLS on every table in any exposed schema, which includes `public` by default. This is critical in Supabase because tables in exposed schemas can be reachable through the Data API when the `anon`/`authenticated` roles have access (see [Exposing a Table to the Data API](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api.md)). For private schemas, prefer RLS as defense in depth. After enabling RLS, create policies that match the actual access model rather than defaulting every table to the same `auth.uid()` pattern.

**6. Security checklist.**
When working on any Supabase task that touches auth, RLS, views, storage, or user data, run through this checklist. These are Supabase-specific security traps that silently create vulnerabilities:

- **Auth and session security**
  - **Never use `user_metadata` claims in JWT-based authorization decisions.** In Supabase, `raw_user_meta_data` is user-editable and can appear in `auth.jwt()`, so it is unsafe for RLS policies or any other authorization logic. Store authorization data in `raw_app_meta_data` / `app_metadata` instead.
  - **Deleting a user does not invalidate existing access tokens.** Sign out or revoke sessions first, keep JWT expiry short for sensitive apps, and for strict guarantees validate `session_id` against `auth.sessions` on sensitive operations.
  - **If you use `app_metadata` or `auth.jwt()` for authorization, remember JWT claims are not always fresh until the user's token is refreshed.**

- **API key and client exposure**
  - **Never expose the `service_role` or secret key in public clients.** Prefer publishable keys for frontend code. Legacy `anon` keys are only for compatibility. In Next.js, any `NEXT_PUBLIC_` env var is sent to the browser.

- **RLS, views, and privileged database code**
  - **Views bypass RLS by default.** In Postgres 15 and above, use `CREATE VIEW ... WITH (security_invoker = true)`. In older versions of Postgres, protect your views by revoking access from the `anon` and `authenticated` roles, or by putting them in an unexposed schema.
  - **UPDATE requires a SELECT policy.** In Postgres RLS, an UPDATE needs to first SELECT the row. Without a SELECT policy, updates silently return 0 rows — no error, just no change.
  - **`auth.role()` is deprecated — use the `TO` clause instead.** Supabase has deprecated `auth.role()` in favour of specifying the target role directly on the policy with `TO authenticated` or `TO anon`. Beyond deprecation, `auth.role() = 'authenticated'` breaks silently when anonymous sign-ins are enabled, because anonymous users carry the `authenticated` Postgres role and pass the check regardless of whether the user is genuinely signed in.
    ```sql
    -- Deprecated (do not use)
    create policy "example" on table_name for select
    using ( auth.role() = 'authenticated' );
    ```
  - **`TO authenticated` alone is authentication without authorization (BOLA / IDOR).** Using `TO authenticated` only checks the role — it does not restrict which rows a user can access. The correct pattern combines `TO authenticated` with an ownership predicate in `USING`:
    ```sql
    create policy "example" on table_name for select
    to authenticated
    using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );
    ```
  - **UPDATE policies require both `USING` and `WITH CHECK`.** Without `WITH CHECK`, a user can reassign a row's `user_id` to another user:
    ```sql
    create policy "example" on table_name for update
    to authenticated
    using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id )
    with check ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );
    ```
  - **`SECURITY DEFINER` functions bypass RLS.** A `SECURITY DEFINER` function runs with its creator's privileges — typically a role with `bypassrls` (e.g., `postgres`). Never add `SECURITY DEFINER` to resolve a permission error; it silently removes access control without fixing the underlying cause. Prefer `SECURITY INVOKER`.
  - **`SECURITY DEFINER` functions in `public` are callable by all roles.** Postgres grants `EXECUTE` to `PUBLIC` by default for every new function, so any `SECURITY DEFINER` function in `public` is a public API endpoint callable by `anon` and `authenticated` (which inherit from `PUBLIC`) without any additional grant. When `SECURITY DEFINER` is genuinely needed (e.g., bypassing RLS on an internal lookup table), keep the function in a non-exposed schema, always include an `auth.uid()` check in the function body, and run `supabase db advisors` after making changes.

- **Storage access control**
  - **Storage upsert requires INSERT + SELECT + UPDATE.** Granting only INSERT allows new uploads but file replacement (upsert) silently fails. You need all three.

- **Dependency and supply-chain security**
  - **Always pin package versions and commit lockfiles** when installing Supabase packages (`supabase-js`, `@supabase/ssr`, `supabase-py`, etc.). See the [npm security guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/security/npm-security.md) for the full checklist.

For any security concern not covered above, fetch the Supabase product security index: `https://supabase.com/docs/guides/security/product-security.md`

## Supabase CLI

Always discover commands via `--help` — never guess. The CLI structure changes between versions.

```bash
supabase --help                    # All top-level commands
supabase <group> --help            # Subcommands (e.g., supabase db --help)
supabase <group> <command> --help  # Flags for a specific command
```

**Supabase CLI Known gotchas:**

- `supabase db query` requires **CLI v2.79.0+** → use MCP `execute_sql` or `psql` as fallback
- `supabase db advisors` requires **CLI v2.81.3+** → use MCP `get_advisors` as fallback
- In imperative migration projects, create new hand-authored migration files with `supabase migration new <name>` first. Never invent a migration filename or rely on memory for the expected format. Declarative schema projects generate migrations from `supabase/schemas/`; see "Making and Committing Schema Changes" below.

**Version check and upgrade:** Run `supabase --version` to check. For CLI changelogs and version-specific features, consult the [CLI documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/cli/introduction) or [GitHub releases](https://github.com/supabase/cli/releases).

## Supabase MCP Server

For setup instructions, server URL, and configuration, see the [MCP setup guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/getting-started/mcp).

**Troubleshooting connection issues** — follow these steps in order:

1. **Check if the server is reachable:**
   `curl -so /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp`
   A `401` is expected (no token) and means the server is up. Timeout or "connection refused" means it may be down.

2. **Check `.mcp.json` configuration:**
   Verify the project root has a valid `.mcp.json` with the correct server URL. If missing, create one pointing to `https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp`.

3. **Authenticate the MCP server:**
   If the server is reachable and `.mcp.json` is correct but tools aren't visible, the user needs to authenticate. The Supabase MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 — tell the user to trigger the auth flow in their agent, complete it in the browser, and reload the session.

## Supabase Documentation

Before implementing any Supabase feature, find the relevant documentation. Use these methods in priority order:

1. **MCP `search_docs` tool** (preferred — returns relevant snippets directly)
2. **Fetch docs pages as markdown** — any docs page can be fetched by appending `.md` to the URL path.
3. **Web search** for Supabase-specific topics when you don't know which page to look at.

## Making and Committing Schema Changes

First decide which schema workflow the project uses.

### Option A: Declarative schemas

Use this when `supabase/schemas/` exists or `config.toml` sets `schema_paths`. Edit the desired schema state in those files, then generate and review the migration. Do not start by hand-writing a migration. See the [Declarative database schemas guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development/declarative-database-schemas).

### Option B: Imperative migrations

Use this when the project does not use declarative schemas.

**To make schema changes, use `execute_sql` (MCP) or `supabase db query` (CLI).** These run SQL directly on the database without creating migration history entries, so you can iterate freely and generate a clean migration when ready.

Do NOT use `apply_migration` to change a local database schema — it writes a migration history entry on every call, which means you can't iterate, and `supabase db diff` / `supabase db pull` will produce empty or conflicting diffs. If you use it, you'll be stuck with whatever SQL you passed on the first try.

**When ready to commit** your changes to a migration file:

1. **Run advisors** → `supabase db advisors` (CLI v2.81.3+) or MCP `get_advisors`. Fix any issues.
2. **Review the Security Checklist above** if your changes involve views, functions, triggers, or storage.
3. **Generate the migration** → `supabase db pull <descriptive-name> --local --yes`
4. **Verify** → `supabase migration list --local`

## Debugging

Source of truth for the FULL rewrite of the old agent backend + wiring the
frontend. Written from `LLM_INSTRUCTIONS.md` + fresh codebase audit (Jan '26
repo state, AGENTS_OLD.md intentionally NOT read).

## Directory

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`NOTES.md`](NOTES.md) | Engineered notes archive (caveman, facts-only) — read this first |
| [`ENV.md`](ENV.md) | All env vars today + new user-suppliable model/key env design |
| [`db/MIGRATION.md`](db/MIGRATION.md) | Snapshot of the OLD schema + migration order (migrate first, then redesign) |
| [`db/SCHEMA.md`](db/SCHEMA.md) | **NEW** full database schema (Supabase, RLS, FKs, indexes) |

| [`PROMPTS.md`](PROMPTS.md) | Single prompt library — one file, all prompts exported+imported |
| [`FEATURES.md`](FEATURES.md) | Feature/tool-call ideas beyond the ask (sub-agents, http tool, media, etc) |
| [`UI.md`](UI.md) | Missing/better UI components + placements |
| [`QUESTIONS.md`](QUESTIONS.md) | Clarification questions for the human |

1. `NOTES.md` → facts.

Old files that were deleted by design (do not revive): `AGENTS_OLD.md`, old
`docs/` architecture, old `internal/` plans.

# NOTES — Facts Archive (caveman)

Engineered notes. Facts from repo audit + docs. Written during exploration to
survive compaction. Code refs `path:line`.

## Stack (live)
- Bun 1.3.9, Turborepo, TS ~6.0, React ^19.2, Next ^16.3, `ai` ^7.0.93
  (`streamText`, `Chat`, `ToolLoopAgent`, `toolApproval`, `stopWhen`),
  `@ai-sdk/react` ^4.0.100 (`useChat`, `DefaultChatTransport`),
  `@ai-sdk/groq` ^4.0.37, tRPC v11, drizzle ^0.45, better-auth 1.7.1,
  inngest ^4.20, mem0ai, zustand (0 stores yet), zod ^4.5.
- Supabase local CLI scaffold exists: `packages/db/supabase/config.toml`,
  `.temp/cli-latest`=v2.117.0, `schema_paths=[]`, migrations enabled,
  `seed/seed.sql` referenced but MISSING. Auth enabled (external google
  defaults off). Storage enabled. `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` +
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` in `apps/web/.env` but UNUSED.
- Harness: pg (node-postgres) via DATABASE_URL/DIRECT_URL. better-auth tables:
  user/session/account/verification. `src/migrations/` has only `.gitkeep` —
  NO real migrations yet.

## Backend pieces (to be replaced)
- `@aevryn/api` tRPC: `agentRouter` muts = sendMessage, confirmWorkflow,
  discardPlan, updateObjective, runWorkflow, stopWorkflow, toggleSchedule,
  deleteSchedule, markNotificationsRead, resolveApproval, deleteMemories,
  deleteAllMemories, pauseWorkflow, resumeWorkflow. Queries = getThread,
  unreadNotifications, listRuns, listNotifications, listApprovals, listMemories.
- `@aevryn/workflow` WorkflowService god class (1517 lines, ~66 methods), 12
  repos, `schemas.ts` (planSchema `{title,objective,summary,steps}`,
  decisionSchema `{action: complete|sleep|notify|stop|wait,...}`),
  Mem0 store null-degrades w/o key.
- `@aevryn/inngest`: functions execution-run (914 lines, idempotent gate,
  regex-extracts ```json plan/decision), notification-notifier, schedule-tick
  (NO trigger — cron dead), served at `/api/inngest` ONLY executionRun.
- `@aevryn/agent`: 13 capabilities (searchWeb, scrapeUrl, crawlSite, mapSite,
  researchTopic, wireAction, browserSessionList/Create/Rename/Delete,
  createSchedule, storeMemory, searchMemory). Registry + runtime
  `generateText` loop w/ toolApproval gate, replay-by-tool-name, inline
  TOOL_SELECTION_INSTRUCTIONS.
- Env server: DATABASE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, BETTER_AUTH_URL,
  ANAKIN_API_KEY/BASE_URL, INNGEST_EVENT_KEY/SIGNING_KEY/APP_ID,
  GROQ_API_KEY, GROQ_MODEL (default `openai/gpt-oss-20b`), MEM0_API_KEY,
  AGENT_MAX_STEPS=5, AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS=50, EXECUTION_MAX_SECONDS=900,
  EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD=1, EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS=604800,
  RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2, WEBHOOK_BASE_URL. web.ts client empty.

## Anakin SDK 0.1.0 (full surface)
- Client: scrape, map, crawl, search, agenticSearch, wire, countries,
  sessions.{list,create,save,update,delete}.
- ScrapeFormat: markdown|html|cleanedHtml|json|links|images|screenshot|
  screenshotFullPage|summary. Document{...screenshotUrl,fullPageScreenshotUrl}.
- Raw PNG download NOT wrapped — need authed GET /v1/url-scraper/{id}/screenshot.
- Unused today: sessions.save (login→save loop), screenshots, json/links/
  images/summary formats, forceFresh, countries/SUPPORTED_COUNTRY_CODES,
  generateJson, polling knobs.
- REST-only (NOT in SDK): batch scrape ≤10 urls, inline scrape, outputSchema
  on scrape, monitors CRUD, ai-visibility, per-request webhook_url + HMAC
  signature, wire catalog/identities/vaults/wire-run(file downloads),
  CDP Browser API (wss browser-connect: click/type/press/mouse/drag/scroll/
  tabs/waits/evaluate/route/intercept + `?save_session=` `?session_id=`).
- Node-only SDK (no browser build). Adapters call only basic methods.

## UI (packages/ui + apps/web)
- ChatComposer: no props, self-contained. value, files[], queue[], status(idle/
  streaming demo), quality slider 0..50000 (labels Free→God), QueuedStack
  drag-reorder/edit/remove, suggestions[4], openFilePicker, accept default
  image/png,image/jpeg,application/pdf. has onQueueChange/onStop.
- ChatMessage props: `{from:"user"|"assistant", files?:File[],
  thumbnailSize=64, time?, actions?, size?}`. NO `attachment` prop — files only;
  FileThumbnail renders. (User hoped for video/image attachment − need to add).
- SystemMessage: `{icon?,isIconHidden?,cta?:{label,onClick,variant}, cva
  variant: action|error|warning, fill?:bool}`.
- ask-user-questions: AskUserQuestion{id,title,options?,multiSelect?,
  allowOther?,otherPlaceholder?,skippable?,nextLabel?,layout:inline|stacked,
  chipPosition:left|right, freeText?,freeTextPlaceholder?,freeTextMultiline?,
  freeTextValidate?}; AskUserOption{id?,title,description?};
  AskUserAnswer{questionId,selectedIds[],otherText?,skipped?}. NEWTODO:37
  says becomes LLM toolcall schema. QuestionFlow wrapper in packages/ui.
- ThinkingSteps: ThinkingStep{icon(IconName),showIcon,label,description?,
  status:complete|active|pending,delay,isLast}, ThinkingStepDetails{summary,
  details:string[]}, ThinkingStepSources/Source{color,...}, ThinkingStepImage
  {src,alt,caption}. ThinkingIndicator animated morph+words.
- tool-step-calls.tsx: mock ResearchAgent/WebScrapeAgent/CompilingAgent/
  FinalAnswerStep — hardcoded ThinkingSteps.
- workspace/page.tsx (567): ALL hardcoded. Header = SearchableDropdown +
  InputGroup rename (no-op) + Run btn + Settings btn (NEWTODO:253 run visible
  after bound workflow). Conversation = mock ChatMessage/QuestionFlow/
  AccordionGroup(items)/Table/SystemMessage(actions)/ThinkingIndicator.
  Footer ChatComposer empty. NEWTODO:338 mb-40.
- Sidebar (packages/ui/app-sidebar.tsx 419, src-slot empty in web):
  workspace switch (Acme Inc/Personal/New), search (Cmd+K), notifications
  btn (Cmd+N, no chip yet), new btn (Cmd+O), NAV_SECTIONS groups w/ add +
  section dropdown (run all/stop all/rename/delete all), items w/ status dot +
  badge, hover run/stop + rename + 3-dot(share/delete), footer settings/
  theme/user row (Jane Doe mock, Profile no-op). nav-data.ts hardcoded.
- searchable-dropdown: hardcoded WORKFLOW_GROUPS. NEWTODO:16,41.
- workflow-dialog (546): SECTIONS general{name, desc, autoApprove switch, delete},
  share{InputCopy mock}, plan{steps editable}, instructions{system prompt only},
  memories{mock}. NEWTODO wants "Agent" tab + env tab for user keys.
- settings-dialog (491): General/Notifications/Appearance/Security/Members.
- notifications-dialog (119): mock 5 {id,content,read}, no mark-all-read.
- No ProfileDialog (menu no-op). No Toaster mounted. providers = Theme,
  SizeContext, QueryClient(+devtools). authClient dead code.
- Notifications unread-chip missing (user: add like thread button).

## User's new rules
- Auth: Google Supabase ONLY for MVP. Pre-signup questions (who are you: student/
  engineer/AI engineer/...) → profile. Root page.tsx = login screen.
- Workspace "PERSONAL" auto-created per user. MVP single workspace. Schema scalable.
- Sidebar: section search by thread title, notifications chip + mark-read-on-open,
  New btn → new workflow GROUP, group dropdown run all/stop all/rename/delete all,
  workflow item name + status icon + hover run/stop/rename/3-dot.
- Header: dropdown (workflows) + inline rename input. Run/Stop btn only if
  workflow BOUND by toolcall. Workflow settings btn.
- Chat: useChat direct; LLM tools (zod+schema+desc); Anakin tool calls → Inngest
  durable; Inngest returns schematic JSON → ThinkingSteps realtime (sub-tasks too,
  e.g. "reading portfolio/about.html/projects.html"). SystemMessage on error/
  warning/retry; new ChatMessage(assistant) only when error/warning/workflow
  stops/restarts — append same message when running. QuestionFlow parent for
  questionflow, workflowbindingapproval, event approval. Plan editable anyplace.
  LLM decides plan yes/no/steps; user approval UI = workflowApproval questions
  (approve/decline/bind-not-run/request-changes). Decline destroys plan.
  Auto-approve switch → auto Approve + system msg "auto approved via settings".
- Queued messages durable (close window safe). ChatComposer center → bottom after
  first msg; route swap `workspace/<threadId>` no reload. Media: image/pdf upload,
  compress image w/o quality loss → supabase storage. Markdown later (table comp
  ready). Mediums: text, image, speech, transcription, video (per model settings).
- sub-agents parallel later (container collects). mem0 per-thread + global tool.
  zustand for client state; keep server components.
- DB: migrate OLD schema → migration file (snapshot) FIRST, then write NEW schema
  w/ FKs + best practices. No docstrings in code. No hardcoding.
- Deliverables: questions.md, features.md, UI file, PROMPTS file (all prompts in
  one place, export/import), final-docs organizing everything. Env analysis.

# ENV — Variables & User-Suppliable Keys

Three layers: **server/infra env** (Vercel/Next server, never client),
**user workspace keys** (entered by user in Workflow Settings → Agent/Env tab,
stored in DB, encrypted), and **per-thread overrides** (rare, optional).

## Existing env (old backend → what to keep)

| Var | Used by (old) | New use |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` / `DIRECT_URL` | drizzle pg | → Supabase project connection string (keep, used by drizzle) |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` / `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | better-auth | **DELETE** (Supabase Auth owns sessions) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | unused today | keep — supabase-js client |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | unused today | keep — anon role for RLS/DATA API |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | — | **ADD** server-only, storage uploads + admin (never NEXT_PUBLIC) |
| `ANAKIN_API_KEY` / `ANAKIN_BASE_URL` | agent adapters | fallback default; user can override per workspace |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` / `GROQ_MODEL` | runtime | fallback defaults; per workspace override |
| `MEM0_API_KEY` | workflow mem0 | fallback; per workspace override |
| `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` / `SIGNING_KEY` / `APP_ID` | inngest client | keep |
| `WEBHOOK_BASE_URL` | webhook-board | keep |
| `AGENT_MAX_STEPS` / `AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS` / `EXECUTION_MAX_SECONDS` / `EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD` / `EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS` / `RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | inngest | keep as server caps (hard ceiling) |

## NEW env (definitive list, final)

```
# --- Supabase ---
DATABASE_URL                # postgres connection for drizzle (direct)
DIRECT_URL                  # pooler direct url (non-pooled, for migrations)
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL    # client
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY  # client anon (never secret)
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY   # server only — storage bucket mgmt, user creation
SUPABASE_AUTH_SECRET        # optional: for verifying webhook JWT from auth hooks

# --- Inngest ---
INNGEST_EVENT_KEY
INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY
INNGEST_APP_ID

# --- Webhook interop ---
WEBHOOK_BASE_URL            # base url for generated /api/v1/hooks/:token urls

# --- Defaults (single fallback key each; user overrides per-workspace in UI) ---
ANAKIN_API_KEY
ANAKIN_BASE_URL             # default https://api.anakin.io/v1
GROQ_API_KEY
GROQ_MODEL                  # default text model, e.g. openai/gpt-oss-20b
MEM0_API_KEY

# --- Server hard caps (clamp user values; not editable by user) ---
AGENT_MAX_STEPS             # default 5      — ceiling
AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS        # default 50     — ceiling
EXECUTION_MAX_SECONDS       # default 900    — ceiling
EXECUTION_MAX_COST_USD      # default 1      — ceiling
EXECUTION_MAX_SLEEP_SECONDS # default 604800 — ceiling
RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS       # default 2      — ceiling

# --- Model routing (per category; fall back from workspace → env default) ---
TEXT_MODEL                   # alias of GROQ_MODEL default (kept by name parity)
IMAGE_MODEL                  # default e.g. groq/text2img or provider, optional
SPEECH_MODEL                 # optional
TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL          # optional
VIDEO_MODEL                  # optional (future)
```

> Client (`packages/env/src/web.ts`) must expose only:
> `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`.
> Everything else stays server-only. `SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION` respected.

## Where the USER enters their own keys (UI)

Primary → **Workflow Settings dialog → "Agent" tab** (rename of
"Instructions"), with an **"Environment"** subsection:

- Groq API key + Groq model (text)
- Anakin API key + base URL
- Mem0 API key
- (secondary) Image / Speech / Transcription / Video model overrides

Stored in DB table `workspace_api_keys`:
`workspace_id | user_id | provider | key_name | key_value(encrypted) | created_at`.

Resolution order at call time: **thread override → workflow/workspace key →
env default**. `workflow_api_keys` optional per-thread override keyed same way.
Encryption: AES-256-GCM with `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env (add to server env) — or
Supabase Vault (`vault.create_secret`) if service_role available. Recommend
**Supabase Vault** — no extra env key, native audit.

## Best placement reasoning
- Workspace is the right scope: keys belong to a workspace, reusable in the
  `PERSONAL` workspace and future ones. Thread-level is pointless UX (user
  shouldn't re-enter per thread); we allow per-thread override but never require.
- Server retains hard caps so a user cannot self-grant unlimited budgets.
- Never ship keys to client — tools run server-side (Inngest/route), so only
  server reads them.
